step_by_step_reasoning:
The architecture diagram and transcript depict HubSpot's asynchronous task queuing system built on top of AWS SQS, EC2 microservices, and external storage engines (Kafka, HBase, MySQL).

1. Node Identification:
- Microservices running on EC2: ENQUEUE (id: 0), UNIQUE (id: 2), SCHEDULER (id: 6), and SCHEDULE WATCHER (id: 9).
- SQS Queues: SQS UNIQUE (id: 1), SQS SCHEDULER (id: 5), and SQS SCHEDULE WATCHER (id: 8).
- External/Third-Party Engines (ThirdParty): KAFKA (id: 3), HBASE (id: 4), and MYSQL (id: 7).

2. Flow Segmentation:
- Flow 0: Task Enqueue & Fallback strategy (ENQUEUE -> SQS UNIQUE / KAFKA fallback cycle).
- Flow 1: Task Uniqueness Check (SQS UNIQUE -> UNIQUE EC2 microservice -> HBase lookup/store -> SQS SCHEDULER).
- Flow 2: Task Scheduling (SQS SCHEDULER -> SCHEDULER EC2 -> MySQL persistence / direct bypass to SQS SCHEDULE WATCHER if within execution window).
- Flow 3: Task Execution Polling (MySQL -> SCHEDULE WATCHER & SQS SCHEDULE WATCHER -> SCHEDULE WATCHER).

graph.name: HubSpot Asynchronous Task Queuing Architecture
graph.notes: HubSpot handles over 6,500 task enqueues per second across a microservice architecture built on AWS SQS, EC2, Kafka, HBase, and MySQL.

nodes.name: ENQUEUE
nodes.notes: Microservice handling incoming task requests (e.g., email dispatch) at around 6,500 tasks/second.

nodes.name: SQS UNIQUE
nodes.notes: Dedicated queue for buffering incoming tasks undergoing uniqueness checking.

nodes.name: UNIQUE
nodes.notes: Microservice that checks task uniqueness against HBase before proceeding.

nodes.name: KAFKA
nodes.notes: Self-managed internal Kafka cluster used as a secondary fallback buffer during SQS timeouts/outages.

nodes.name: HBASE
nodes.notes: NoSQL data store used to hold and check namespace-isolated task uniqueness IDs.

nodes.name: SQS SCHEDULER
nodes.notes: Queue holding validated unique tasks awaiting scheduling.

nodes.name: SCHEDULER
nodes.notes: Microservice responsible for saving scheduled tasks into MySQL or forwarding ready tasks directly.

nodes.name: MYSQL
nodes.notes: Relational database used to store future-scheduled tasks beyond SQS's native 15-minute delay limit.

nodes.name: SQS SCHEDULE WATCHER
nodes.notes: Queue storing ready-to-execute tasks for consumption.

nodes.name: SCHEDULE WATCHER
nodes.notes: Worker microservice reading ready tasks from SQS SCHEDULE WATCHER or polling due tasks from MySQL.

edges.notes: ENQUEUE sends incoming tasks to SQS UNIQUE.
Fallback path: ENQUEUE produces messages to Kafka if SQS is unavailable or times out.
Worker reads fallback messages from Kafka back into the enqueue process once SQS recovers.
UNIQUE microservice consumes task messages from SQS UNIQUE queue.
UNIQUE microservice checks HBase for task ID existence to filter out duplicates.
Verified unique tasks are forwarded to SQS SCHEDULER queue.
SCHEDULER microservice pulls tasks from SQS SCHEDULER queue.
SCHEDULER writes long-term scheduled tasks to MySQL database.
Fast-path: SCHEDULER bypasses MySQL write and sends task directly to SQS SCHEDULE WATCHER if execution time is within 15 minutes.
SCHEDULE WATCHER polls due tasks from MySQL when their execution time window is reached.
SCHEDULE WATCHER pulls ready-to-execute task messages from SQS SCHEDULE WATCHER.
